reviews.review:
No game will ever capture the power of a Space Marine. Hell even the sound of you running makes a resonating BOOM that carries weight to the world around you.

The multiplayer may be dead, but the single player is still a rich and rampant experience.

Crush Orks beneath your mighty heel, chainsaw chaos demons in two or if you are so inclined get a power hammer and do most of those things AT ONCE.

Beautiful environments rich in the design of 40k, weapons that feel authentic and suprising voice acting that lends to the regality of the Adeptus Astrates. A grand experience I will keep coming back to until another that can match its quality rises to face it.

Story:It's servicable. Nothing great but at the same time nothing that will make your braincells implode.
Graphics:Graphics both from a fidelity and art design perspective do their jobs. Tho it is quite impressive how the developers didn't shy away from putting a bilion of enemies on screen and making it not run like a complete turd(aka gud port).
Sound and music: Again decent enough.
Gameplay: The gameplay basically consist of you running into a big open area and killing hordes of enemies. The fighting system can be divided into segments the shooting and the melee combat. I'll start with the gunplay. The guns do feel quite satisfying to use. They feel chunky and powerful and your given a decent number of them to keep things interesting. The melee is also quite enjoyable and same as the fire arms your given different types of melee weapons to play around with it.
Now given that there are two approaches to the combat you'd think that your presented with the choice on how you want to dispose of your enemies but that's the problem really. When your playing this game on hard the guns become almost mendatory and the melee takes a step back, being rendered as situational. Plus the third act of this game will make you want to die. The enemies become so bullet spongy and you take so much damage even when you have your shields fully upgraded. But that's the singleplayer as for the multiplayer it's pretty standard stuff: team death match, capture the flag, etc. Though there is a horde mode which can be pretty fun with a couple of buddies.
Conclusion: To end this, the game is just slightly above average. It's one of those type of games you play when you have some down time. Is it worth buying? I'd say yes especially with the price tag it has now.

This is by far the most immersive 40k game, but it's riddled with flaws, namely its extremely linear gameplay and repetitiveness. The multiplayer is viciously lacking. Take this style of game and open it up to a more expansive multiplayer and a more open world, and you'll have something awesome.
One of the best game for W40k the atmosphere is so good
